title: Burst coalescer + kernel-parameter sweep to lower embedding p99
creator: Maya Chen
description: We observe a persistent high tail (p99) on the embeddings endpoint during brief request bursts from customer workloads. Initial analysis shows many requests that arrive within 5–30ms of each other are being dispatched as separate GPU kernels, causing underfilled kernel launches and higher p99. This ticket explores a two-pronged approach: a lightweight in-memory burst coalescer to opportunistically group near-simultaneous requests and a systematic kernel-parameter sweep (thread/block/tiling heuristics and cuBLAS/cuDNN algorithm hints) to reduce per-request overhead when coalescing is imperfect.
acceptance_criteria: 1) p99 for a synthetic bursty workload reduces by >=25% compared to baseline within staging; 2) end-to-end median remains within 5% of baseline for single-request latency; 3) no increased GPU memory OOMs in 24h soak test; 4) rollout plan with gradual traffic ramp and rollback criteria documented.
implementation_notes:
Plan:
- Implement ephemeral burst coalescer in front of per-GPU queue (window=8ms, adaptive up to 25ms under load), with opt-out per-tenant flag.
- Add instrumentation hooks to measure coalesce-size histogram, kernel occupancy, and per-request queuing delay.
- Run automated kernel-parameter sweep across representative models (embed-small, embed-medium) to find lower-overhead launch configs. Parameters: block_size candidates [32,64,128], quantization code-paths (fp16, int8), cuBLAS algo preferences where applicable.
- Safety: enforce max coalesced batch size and fallback to single-request path if memory pressure crosses threshold.
- Eval: synthetic burst driver that simulates real customer burst patterns (Poisson baseline with occasional 200–500 req/s spikes).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy current staging runtime. 2) Run provided burst-driver (scripts/burst_driver.py) targeting embed-small with burst pattern (baseline 50 rps, spike to 400 rps for 10s every 60s). 3) Capture p50/p95/p99 from console-collector, and trace a sample of kernel launches using perf markers. 4) Observe separate kernel launches for requests arriving within 10ms.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for coalescer correctness (ordering, time-window semantics).
- Microbenchmarks for each kernel param set with sample sequences and KV-cache hits/misses.
- 24h soak test on staging with production-like traffic replay.
- Canary rollout: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% within a day, with automated rollback on p99 regressions >10% or error-rate increase >0.5%.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: coalescing increases queuing delay harming single-request latency. Mitigation: adaptive window tuned to keep median within 5% of baseline and tenant opt-out flag. Risk: new kernel params may regress throughput for long sequences; mitigation: limit config per model family and keep experiment flags.
